grid.origin: north-west corner; x east, y south; cell (i, j) covers map units [i*0.5, i*0.5+0.5) x [j*0.5, j*0.5+0.5); row j is rows[j]

elevation.fromAtlas: land: m = 750*h + 2600*max(0, h-0.5)^1.4 where h is the atlas relief (hgt in render()), averaged over 4x4 atlas pixels; sea: depth from the distance to the coast, -(5 + 120*smooth(0,4,d) + 1600*smooth(4,25,d)) m; carved passes lowered as listed in passes[]
elevation.water: shallow hollows drained by cutting their outlets (1456 cells lowered, at most 916 m); the rest are lakes (lakes[]): rows give the lake floor, lakes[].surfaceM the water

biomes.note: base terrain = the atlas biome (region terrain, chosen by the atlas noise); alpine = above the treeline, snow = above the snowline, beach = the atlas sandy rim, lake = filled depressions

regions.note: character k in a row = legend[index of k in "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABC"]; "." = sea

climate.seaLevelTempC: T(y) = 0.28*y (y in map units, 0 = north); lapse 6.5 C per km of height
climate.snowline: permanent snow where T < -5 C (and above 900 m; never on volcanic or demon ground); winter snow comes about 1000 m lower
climate.treeline: trees thin out where T < -1 C (above 700 m)

detail.note: Added layer (rivers[].pathCells/pathSmooth/order/endsIn, settlements[], roads[]). Older fields are unchanged. Generated by Tools/atlas/build_physical_map.js; docs 10_World/physical_geography.md §11.
detail.rivers: rivers[].path keeps the simplified cell points; rivers[].pathCells is every cell centre [x,y] km; rivers[].pathSmooth is [x km, y km, water level m, width m, Strahler stream order] every ~0.25 km from source to mouth (water level never rises downstream; tributaries end on their parent; main rivers end one sea cell offshore at 0 m); rivers[].order is the highest stream order; rivers[].endsIn says where it ends.
detail.settlements: settlements[]: id, name, region, x/y km, elevationM (the heightmap, bilinear on elevation.rows, so it sits on the terrain mesh), fineElevationM (atlas relief at 0.125 km), maxSlope300mPct (steepest gradient of the fine atlas relief within 300 m, percent), kind, ring0, inWater (sea|lake|null), source, gazetteer text.
detail.roads: roads[]: one per land leg of the five corridors; points are [x km, y km, heightmap m] every ~0.25 km; connects lists settlement ids within 0.75 km of the line in travel order; crossings are river crossings; approachKm is the length of the lead-in from the corridor route to each end settlement (not held to the 2,000 m pass limit; highestM, climbM and maxGradePct cover the corridor route only).

settlements.name: terrace cities
settlements.gazetteer: Cities of fitted stone built on the terraces, linked by stone roads and relay huts.

settlements.name: Ashira
settlements.gazetteer: A warm, welcoming town of bridges and gardens on the river, where everyone is happy.

settlements.name: Bastion outer ring
settlements.gazetteer: The outermost ring of walls, its villages and fields, the front line of the siege.

settlements.name: Cinderhole
settlements.gazetteer: The city in the smoking crater, built into its walls and the caves behind them.

settlements.name: dragon-bone monasteries
settlements.gazetteer: Monasteries built into the great bones along the Bone Road, with the Skull at their head.

settlements.name: the town on Thalassa's back
settlements.gazetteer: A town of rope, timber and canvas lashed to the hide of a sand-whale, home of the Whale's Belly inn.

settlements.name: Summer Court glades
settlements.gazetteer: The last glades of the Summer Court, warm and golden, home of the Hour That Isn't.

settlements.name: Fanghold
settlements.gazetteer: The stone fortress above the Deep Well, and the market town around it, home of the Howling Hearth inn.

settlements.name: nomad yurt camps
settlements.gazetteer: Moving camps of felt yurts that follow the herds across the steppe.

settlements.name: longhouse steads
settlements.gazetteer: Clan farms of long turf-roofed houses scattered along the fjords.

settlements.name: Skjaldheim
settlements.gazetteer: The great hold at the head of the longest fjord, home of the Last Fire inn.

settlements.name: Gearholm Undercity
settlements.gazetteer: The tunnels, boilers and slums beneath the mountain, home of the city's labourers and of the Great Engines.

settlements.name: pirate stilt-towns
settlements.gazetteer: Towns on stilts on the outer reefs, joined by rope bridges and governed by elected captains.

settlements.name: Port Goldmere
settlements.gazetteer: The salvage port, a town of ship-timber houses around a deep harbour, home of the Drowned Mermaid inn.

settlements.name: Greymoor stilt-village
settlements.gazetteer: The largest of the fen's villages, built on ironwood stilts around the Crooked Lantern inn.

settlements.name: the Walking Hut market
settlements.gazetteer: A trader's hut on great bird legs that walks a slow circuit of the fen; where it stops, there is a market.

settlements.name: Haneul gate-towns
settlements.gazetteer: Terraced towns climbing the pass, the capital at the top with its Cloud Gate Guesthouse.

settlements.name: Heavenfolk eyries
settlements.gazetteer: Homes carved into the south-facing cliffs, linked by flight paths and reached by the Long Stair.

settlements.name: Bamboo Sea villages
settlements.gazetteer: Villages in the bamboo forests, the first to fall under Kurogane's masks.

settlements.name: Hoshizora City
settlements.gazetteer: The capital at the river mouth, with its castle, temples and the Ryokan Moon-on-Water.

settlements.name: Ashen Mines camps
settlements.gazetteer: Mining camps of dwarves and hired labourers in the eastern seams, now held by Skarn's army.

settlements.name: Karak Dûn
settlements.gazetteer: The great dwarven hold carved into the mountain's heart, entered through the Khazdûr Gate and home of the Anvil's Rest inn.

settlements.name: Fox Shrine Isle
settlements.gazetteer: The main island, with the great fox shrine and the Ninth Tail Teahouse.

settlements.name: spirit inns
settlements.gazetteer: Inns run by spirits across the isles, where humans are guests and contracts are law.

settlements.name: Lirian canal cities
settlements.gazetteer: A cluster of island cities joined by bridges and canals, with the doge's palace at their centre.

settlements.name: Lumbaya temple villages
settlements.gazetteer: Villages built among the ruins of the old temples, deep in the jungle.

settlements.name: Lustrine glass beaches
settlements.gazetteer: Villages on the dunes above the glowing beaches.

settlements.name: Moraveil goblin village
settlements.gazetteer: A cliff village of caves and ladders, home of the Friendly Goblin inn.

settlements.name: Moraveil market town
settlements.gazetteer: A busy human market town on the river, joined to the goblin village by the Truce Bridge.

settlements.name: Thimblefolk Mushroom Town
settlements.gazetteer: A town of hollowed toadstools and grass bridges, home of the Thimble & Thistle inn.

settlements.name: Stiller spring-towns
settlements.gazetteer: Towns of wood and rope built around the still springs.

settlements.name: sect foothill towns
settlements.gazetteer: Towns at the feet of the sect mountains, where disciples buy supplies and villagers sell them, near the Jade Crossroads and the Wandering Dragon Inn.

settlements.name: Stormreach cliff-towns
settlements.gazetteer: Towns bolted to the cliffs above the sea, crowned with lightning rods.

settlements.name: border baronies
settlements.gazetteer: Small fortified towns and manors ruled by quarrelling barons.

settlements.name: mercenary forts
settlements.gazetteer: Timber and stone forts where the sellsword companies wait for their next contract.

settlements.name: Oasis of Qadira
settlements.gazetteer: The green oasis around seven wells, with palm groves, gardens and the Oasis Caravanserai.

settlements.name: Canopy City Lothaniel
settlements.gazetteer: The court city high in the canopy, a maze of halls and bridges grown from living wood, home of Leafhall Rest.

settlements.name: Moonwell hamlets
settlements.gazetteer: Wood-elf villages on the forest floor, built around glowing pools, now the first in the blight's path.

settlements.name: Naming Voyage harbor
settlements.gazetteer: The harbour on the largest island, where the Naming Voyages begin.

settlements.name: Velmark ducal towns
settlements.gazetteer: White stone towns of markets, banks and courts, each ruled by a duke.

settlements.name: Vharlen frontier legions
settlements.gazetteer: The garrison towns, forts and legion camps along the frontier and the capital behind them, home of the Imperial Grand Hotel.

settlements.name: Brindlewick
settlements.gazetteer: A timber village where most adventurers wake up for the first time in Aethwyrd, home of the guild branch and the Sleeping Griffon inn.

settlements.name: Millbrook
settlements.gazetteer: A mill town on the Millbrook stream with a working waterwheel, a cheese cellar and a stubborn council of millers.

settlements.name: ice-fishing villages
settlements.gazetteer: Villages that move between the rocks and the ice with the seasons.

settlements.name: Xochitl river-cities
settlements.gazetteer: River-cities of reed and carved stone on islands in the lagoons, linked by canoe-roads and flower markets.

settlements.name: Zaruma gold-road towns
settlements.gazetteer: Rich towns of mud-brick towers, libraries and markets at the wells along the gold road.

settlements.name: Zarvan garden cities
settlements.gazetteer: Terraced cities of gardens, fountains and universities, fed by the great aqueducts.
